readingMethod: Read all 39 RU/EN pairs in original story order, inspected the actual HTML's sole effective JSON corpus and renderer, and verified complete screen/source/method parity. Read Essential/Core from actual embedded prose, then all nine Deep insertions in their full 39-screen sequence and neighboring transitions. conclusion: A faithful selective thematic condensation of Marcus's self-addressed reflections, arguments and concrete examples. Retained moral reasoning and the religious/cosmological frame survive. Important retained passages remain in actual translator wording rather than generic advice.

screenReviews.assessment: Accurate framing of recurring self-address; no dated-diary or reconstructed life scene.
Family/teacher debts and admitted failure follow I.1–3,7,17. Admission belongs within I.17, not its final words; optional precision only.
Non-performance, simple letters, attentive reading and Epictetus in I.7; calm with affection and care for friends in I.9.
I.16 supplies deliberation, voluntary friendship, public spending, bodily care and comfort without dependence.
V.1 contains reluctance, bedclothes, working creatures, measured rest and social work compared with craft devotion.
II.1 connects difficult people to ignorance, shared reason/divinity and co-operation; moral non-corruption is not physical immunity.
II.2,8 support body/breath/ruling part, resistance to unsocial impulses and attention to one's own mind.
II.14 supplies the present-possession argument; actual IV.17 scan wording is retained, not a popular paraphrase.
II.2–3 directly support setting books aside, age, nature, accepted principles and gratitude to gods.
IV.3 links inward retreat to ordered principles and a return without discontent; no withdrawal from social duty.
IV.4's chain from common intelligence/reason to law, fellow citizenship and world-state is retained.
IV.40 and VII.9 support the living universe, one soul/substance, god/law/reason; attributed cosmology.
VI.10 and XII.14 retain alternatives rather than identifying providence, necessity and chaos or claiming scientific proof.
III.2 supplies cracked bread, split figs, near-rotten olives, grain, lion's brow and aged beauty in context.
VIII.47 is an actual Marcus claim followed by disposition, action and stronger obstruction; no added recovery guarantee.
VI.13 supplies food bodies, grape juice, purple wool/shellfish dye and deceptive prestige.
IV.49 follows the promontory image with tests of justice, prudence, truth and noble endurance; no magical protection.
V.20 distinguishes obstructed activity from conditional and adaptable disposition while retaining duties to people.
VI.50 contains persuasion, action required by justice, opposing force, another virtue and conditional effort.
VI.30/I.16 support the imperial self-warning and Antoninus's concrete example; no ruler worship.
VI.21 explicitly welcomes correction and opposes persistent error; wording and section correct despite missing Gutenberg HTML anchor.
VI.54's bee/swarm and VI.44's Rome/world citizenship support social good rather than private success.
VII.22's kinship, ignorance, mortality and unchanged ruling faculty retain Marcus's moral reasoning.
VI.20 is an exercise illustration, not an asserted personal accident; caution remains without hatred.
VIII.59 and IX.11 retain teaching/indulgence and gods' gifts of health, wealth and reputation, without a protection promise.
XI.18 reminders 1–5 retained in order: relation/governance, opinions, involuntary error, own faults, uncertain judgment.
XI.18 reminders 6–10 retained in order: brevity, judgment, anger's added harm, sincere kindness, no personal exemption.
IX.1 links social nature to impiety of injustice/lying and pleasure/pain; religious as well as ethical frame survives.
IV.24 revises few tasks to necessary social action and removes unnecessary thoughts; no modern productivity system.
IX.29 retains Plato's Republic, small improvement, unchanged opinions and coerced/pretended obedience.
IV.20,33 support intrinsic worth/emerald and forgotten names; their argument is attributed rather than certified as literal universal oblivion.
VII.48's borrowed elevated view and catalogue of contraries support the prose; Rogovin explicitly has funerals.
IX.40 retains the severe child/loss prayer and divine help even in human power; no guaranteed preservation of loved ones.
V.9 retains failure, returning, most conduct consistent with nature, love of the return and medicinal comparison.
VII.54, VIII.36 and IX.6 support present judgment, social conduct, acceptance and limiting the burden to now.
X.16's exact self-admonition is connected fairly to I.7 and VI.30 rather than turned into an editor's motivational exercise.
III.3 and IV.5 support mortal physicians/commanders/philosophers, voyage, gods/no sensation alternatives and elemental dissolution.
Common XII.36/Rogovin XII.35 supplies actor, three/five acts and nature's limit; no invented final living scene.
Actual closing wording retained separately for both translators, with public XII.36/XII.35 concordance; textual ending, not claimed deathbed statement.

xi18Reminders.retained: People exist for one another; his governing role.
Their daily life and the power of their opinions.
Right conduct does not warrant anger; wrong conduct stems from ignorance.
His own errors and unworthy motives that may have restrained other faults.
Insufficient knowledge to judge another's action confidently.
Another's deed differs from his judgment of it.
Sincere kindness and correction without mockery, rancor or spectators' approval.
It is impossible to abolish others' wrongdoing; exemption for oneself is tyrannical.
